> [bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25619502/bug.zip)

It's not a valid project, there's no `project.godot` file included.

> ### Steps to reproduce
> 
> "Observed a visual mismatch in the property list upon node selection."

Also please provide more detailed steps (you can edit your comment instead of adding another one). Something like:
1. Open MRP.
2. Open scene `X`.
3. Do `something`.
4. (...)
5. Observe the unexpected/buggy behavior.

Simply appending the property list of a custom Resource class to the property list of a Node is meaningless.

Regardless of whether your use case is appropriate, please first compare the differences between `get_property_list()` in the two scripts. The differences have been documented.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1aaea38e7f8dd9e2a94e2e339247fc976a84de75/doc/classes/Object.xml#L684

> [b]注：[/b] 在 GDScript 中，所有类成员都被视为属性。在 C# 和 GDExtension 中，可能需要用装饰器或属性显式标记类成员为 Godot 属性。



> get_property_list()

"I apologize for my limited English; I am using an AI to assist my communication. I have more precise findings to share after further testing:

C# is perfectly fine: In all my tests, C# never exhibits this bug. It consistently and correctly filters out the internal property (ComputeNodeGD), keeping it hidden as expected even after an editor restart.

The bug is exclusive to GDScript and triggered by restart:

Initial State: Immediately after I modify the C# code and perform the first compilation, GDScript still behaves correctly (the internal property remains hidden).

The Trigger: The bug only appears in GDScript after I restart the Godot Editor. Once restarted, GDScript incorrectly exports and displays ComputeNodeGD in the Inspector, while the C# version remains correctly hidden.

The Inconsistency: Despite get_property_list() returning an identical list for both languages, the Inspector handles the GDScript version differently during the editor's startup initialization.
